evaluation_limitations: No independent retrieved chunks, source passages, or retrieval logs were supplied, so corpus fidelity cannot be independently scored.
Illusory correlation and anchoring bias were adjudicated as near-neighbor labels rather than approved aliases of the hidden benchmark labels; this affects strict but not mechanism-first scoring.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I'm the QA analyst covering statistical process control ... Range chart was still flat, so whatever was happening wasn't blowing up part-to-part variability, just shifting the average.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant interprets the chart pattern and distinguishes a mean shift from increased within-subgroup variability, but no hidden bias instance is manifested.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Honestly, at 62% through the shift's quota ... I didn't have an obvious explanation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant gives a reasonable Western Electric assessment of a warning-zone point and trend without committing to an unsupported cause.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I tightened up sampling instead of pulling the trigger on a full stop ... I knew it was real.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant uses increased sampling and a manual spot check as proportionate process-control actions; neither is a hidden bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I could have shut it down right there ... Increasing sampling was the middle path — get more data fast without committing to downtime.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The alternatives and the moderate sampling choice are the intended non-bias response at decision point 1.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I pulled up everything I had access to in real time ... this was the first time he'd seen a pattern like this line up with a temperature swing on this particular machine.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This segment records the available temperature, lot, tool-wear, and engineer information; the hidden correlation occurrence is localized to the subsequent choice to favor temperature and defer the lot test.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The timing just lined up so cleanly on its own ... I put my attention on documenting the temperature correlation and kept monitoring under that assumption.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats temporal co-occurrence as sufficient support for the temperature explanation and does not test the comparably available material-lot hypothesis with equivalent rigor, despite lacking engineer precedent.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The tool wear sensor data finally came through ... Knowing changeover was close made me want to avoid committing to a full stop until the evidence was overwhelming.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant acknowledges strong 78% tool-wear evidence but remains influenced by the recently-serviced-tool assumption and chooses only a small offset rather than a tool change.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The next sample still trended toward the lower spec limit, so the offset wasn't holding ... a cue I obviously didn't have access to until after the handoff.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a consequence and information-availability update after the offset decision, not a separate hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: By the end, several parts were near or slightly under the lower spec limit ... a deviation report was required regardless of what I concluded about the cause.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The final recommendation is the intended accurate tool-change and deviation-report response at decision point 4.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: root-cause hypothesis formation and attribution of dimensional drift to temperature
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Causal inference drawn from temporal co-movement of temperature and dimensional drift, with a comparably available material-lot explanation left untested at the same rigor level; in this variant the inference must rest on timing alone.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Illusory correlation is a related construct describing perceived association from co-occurrence, but it is not treated here as an established alias of the benchmark's Correlation bias label because the benchmark label encodes the broader causal-attribution and evidence-selection instance.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the defining temporal-co-occurrence inference, the temperature-versus-material-lot context, and the failure to test the alternative with equivalent rigor. The mechanism is therefore full even though the label is a near-neighbor.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted Participant statements are verbatim and directly support the mechanism. The retrospective confidence probe is valid corroboration but is not needed to establish the occurrence; the contemporaneous causal-attribution statement is sufficient.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: interpreting 78% tool wear and choosing an intervention
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Underweighting new tool-wear sensor evidence relative to the prior belief that the tool was recently replaced and unlikely to be worn, resulting in a corrective action smaller than the updated evidence justified.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring bias is a near-neighbor construct involving insufficient adjustment from an initial belief, but it is not treated as an approved alias of the benchmark's Conservatism Bias label for strict scoring.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding identifies the recently-serviced-tool belief as the anchor, the contradictory 78% sensor evidence, the time-pressure context, and the smaller-than-justified offset response. This fully captures the hidden belief-updating mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted Participant statements are verbatim, correctly attributed, and directly localize the initial belief, contradictory sensor reading, and insufficiently escalated response. The finding appropriately notes that time pressure contributed without treating time pressure alone as the bias.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The finding is correctly localized and uses valid evidence, but confirmation bias is not the hidden target label and the mechanism omits the defining temporal-co-occurrence causal inference. It captures the untested alternative as an overlapping evidence-selection issue, so it is a partial-mechanism near miss rather than an exact hidden-instance match.

This audit does not alter primary detection or classification scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate findings changes segment detection from 0/2 hits to 2/2 and mechanism-first instance F1 from 0.0000 to 0.8000, while strict instance F1 remains 0.0000; the three moderate findings also create three strict instance false positives.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: There are no low-confidence identified findings, so this increment is zero and all metrics remain unchanged.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: There are no candidate findings, so this increment is zero and all metrics remain unchanged.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At high_only, both positive segments are missed. At high_and_moderate and above, both positive segments are detected with no segment-level false alarms, producing segment F1 of 1.0000.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: No hidden instance receives an exact label-plus-mechanism match: both relevant findings use near-neighbor labels, and the extra confirmation-bias finding is only a partial-mechanism match. Strict F1 is 0.0000 at every threshold.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Both hidden mechanisms are correctly localized with full mechanism overlap at moderate and above. The extra confirmation-bias finding remains a mechanism-first false positive, yielding precision 0.6667, recall 1.0000, and F1 0.8000.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidate biases were supplied, so the candidate tier adds no evidence or scoring change.
main_failure_modes: Both hidden occurrences were assigned near-neighbor rather than benchmark target labels.
The confirmation-bias finding is an additional partial-mechanism prediction rather than a distinct hidden occurrence.
All findings were only moderate confidence, causing complete detection failure at the high-only threshold.
Claimed retrieved support for two findings cannot be independently verified from the supplied inputs.
main_strengths: All three findings use valid, correctly attributed interview quotations.
The two hidden mechanisms were localized to the correct positive segments and captured with full mechanism overlap.
The RAG did not fabricate findings in negative segments or supply candidates that would add false alarms.
The correlation analysis correctly recognized that timing alone, without engineer precedent, drove the participant's attribution.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This counterfactual run supports the intended causal test: the temperature-attribution pattern persisted without the engineer's corroborating anecdote. The RAG detected both positive episodes at moderate confidence, but ontology and over-detection errors separate perfect segment-level performance from zero strict label-plus-mechanism performance.
